questions.question: Which declares a named object shape?
options: class State { name: string; capital: string } only. interface is runtime.
interface State { name: string; capital: string }
interface State = { name: string; capital: string }
questions.explanation: interface names an object type. type can too, with a type alias.

questions.question: Is this type alias roughly the same shape as that interface?
options: Yes. In most everyday object cases they are interchangeable.
Yes, but TState exists at runtime and State does not.
questions.explanation: Item 13: the line has blurred. Either works for a simple object. Know the remaining differences.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.question: Which can declaration-merge two blocks with the same name?
options: class Window twice in one file.
questions.explanation: Interfaces merge. Type aliases with the same name in one scope are an error. Merging is how you augment Window.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.question: What does Admin extend User add?
options: level, plus the fields from User.
Only level; id and name are dropped.
questions.explanation: extends on interfaces is type composition, not a JS prototype.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.code:
interface User { id: number; name: string }
interface Admin extends User { level: number }

questions.question: Does a class need implements User to be assignable to User?
options: No. If the instance shape matches, it is assignable. implements is an assertion.
Yes for public fields, no for methods.
implements emits a runtime interface object.
questions.explanation: implements checks the class against the shape. Structural typing still works without it.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.question: Which needs type, not interface?
options: A object with two string fields.
A method list on a public API object.
An object you might declaration-merge later.
questions.explanation: Unions cannot be interfaces. Use type for unions, tuples, and computed types.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.code:
type Id = string | number;
const id: Id = 12;

questions.question: Which is a tuple alias?
options: interface Pair { 0: string; 1: number } is preferred over a tuple.
questions.explanation: Tuples are type aliases. Interfaces describe object shapes.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.code:
type Pair = [string, number];
const p: Pair = ["Ada", 1];

questions.question: How do you type a method on an interface?
questions.explanation: Method syntax or a function property: onChange: (value: string) => void.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.question: What is a function property versus a method in the interface?
options: There is no difference in the type.
onChange: (value: string) => void is a property holding a function; greet() is a method.
Methods exist at runtime; properties do not.
questions.explanation: Both are callable. The syntax records whether you think of it as a method or a stored function.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.question: Can two type aliases named State merge?
options: No. Duplicate type names in one scope are an error.
Yes if both are object types.
questions.explanation: Declaration merging is an interface feature.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.code:
type State = { name: string };
type State = { capital: string };

questions.question: interface Both extends User, Timestamped means what?
options: A union of User and Timestamped.
questions.explanation: Multiple extends lists compose like an intersection of object types.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.question: Which should you pick for a public object API that others may augment?
options: interface, because it can merge and extend cleanly.
questions.explanation: Interfaces are the usual choice for object APIs. type for unions and computed types.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.question: Does a class also introduce a value?
options: No. class is type-only, like interface.
Yes. A class is a runtime value and a type. interface is type-only.
Yes, and interface also emits a constructor.
questions.explanation: Item 13 mentions class as a third option that exists at runtime. interface does not.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.question: Which callable interface is legal?
options: interface Formatter { (value: string): string; locale: string }
questions.explanation: Call signatures live in the interface body. The value is both callable and has locale.

reference.book: Effective TypeScript, 2nd Edition by Dan Vanderkam
reference.excerpt: If you want to define a named type in TypeScript, you have two options.

questions.question: What does implements check?
options: That the class is a subclass in the JS prototype chain.
That instances of the class are assignable to the interface.
That the interface exists at runtime.
questions.explanation: implements is a static assertion. It does not change the emitted JavaScript.

questions.question: Write makeUser(id, name) returning { id, name }.
questions.explanation: That value satisfies interface User { id: number; name: string } structurally.
